titre: Unofficial GTA 6 PC race is the "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever," says former Destiny 2 dev
chapo: The ex-Bungie dev speculates those involved could be spending thousands of dollars on their AI usage

The ex-Bungie dev speculates those involved could be spending thousands of dollars on their AI usage As vibe coders desperately hurl commands at AI in an attempt to get GTA 6 running on PC, one former Destiny 2 dev says it's led to the "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever" – one that, like a car crash, is hard to look away from. Since notorious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek dropped an Xbox build of the game last week – and more recently followed up with its executable file – multiple groups have been racing to get Rockstar's latest blockbuster up and running on PC. After all, it only launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, so there's a gap there for people without a console that folks have been desperate to fill – though I can't help but think that some hoping for their success might just be keen for a way to play GTA 6 for free. Anyway, it was always inevitable that people would try this, but the way they've been going about it has been messy, to say the least. We've already observed vibe coders begging their AI models of choice to do the GTA 6 port for them, "make no mistakes," and do it "faster," and former gameplay capture artist at Bungie, Amy Hendricks, has also been watching on in dumbfounded awe, documenting what she calls "the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever" in a thread on Bluesky. She first looks at "the slopfest" she calls Project Leonida – one of the frontrunning decompilation projects that yesterday saw its Discord server completely disappear after Rockstar apparently got in touch, and its 15-year-old lead quit (though they've since told followers to "ignore" those posts, so who knows what's going on there). Before that, Hendricks documented: "One group feels like the chatbot developers are not moving fast enough (One reason being the main dev is still at school), so they're going to split the main GTA 6 recomp team into two via forking." Not long after that, fears began that Rockstar and Take-Two were on the way. titre: AI-generated GTA 6 PC ports get nuked in alleged Rockstar takedown spree, as former Bungie dev hails "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"
chapo: One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. extrait: One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-important executable file, which was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek. As documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools. Going by Hendricks's posts, which are based on watching a Leonida stream, much of the recomp's creation seems to have consisted of one or more high school kids typing prompts like "work faster", while spending hundreds or thousands of dollars in usage fees. The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds. In posts preserved by cheery RPS fanzine PCGamer, NotRexed shared a snapshot of a copyright infringement takedown notification from Discord. They explained their decision to call it quits as follows: "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." I myself am a middle aged man, but don't despair, NotRexed! I am not going to yell at you. I am simply going to reach for a moderately small violin. As reported by PCG, the Leonida Discord server has now been shut down, and the Github repository for the recompilation's code has been nuked. Hendricks has shared an alleged takedown request from a representative of Take-Two Interactive, according to which Github have taken action against 3,007 forks (that is, duplicates for the purposes of making a separate version) from the original Leonida repo.
